summary: Exfoliating toner that many reviewers say smooths texture, clears pores and brightens, and a large share use it on the body, scalp or underarms. On the face, irritation and stinging are the main complaints, with breakouts for some, and many limit it to once or twice a week. Some also find it sticky.

Cheap serum that many reviewers credit with less oil, clearer pores and more even tone. The main complaint is breakouts, followed by irritation and stinging for a good number of users. Some find it sticky or prone to pilling under moisturizer or makeup, and many tolerate it better as a few drops mixed into moisturizer.

Short-contact peel that many reviewers say leaves skin smoother, brighter and clearer, usually used weekly or less. Irritation and stinging are the main complaints, and many apply it to dry skin for only a few minutes. A few feel nothing or see little change, and several prefer it on feet.

Leave-on exfoliant that many reviewers credit with clearing clogged pores and blackheads and smoothing texture, often used just a few times a week. Some find it irritating or drying, a smaller group break out, and several dislike an oily, tacky film. Tolerance varies, even among sensitive skin types.

Non-foaming, creamy cleanser that many reviewers find very gentle and comfortable on dry or sensitive skin, often preferring it to CeraVe's. The biggest complaint is burning or stinging for a sizable group, sometimes starting with a new bottle, plus irritation or breakouts for others. Some feel it does not clean well enough alone.

Soothing, rich balm that many reviewers use on dry, irritated or barrier-stressed skin, often at night or alongside tretinoin. The main downside is breakouts for a good number of users, especially with oily or acne-prone skin, plus a heavy, greasy feel. Several say a newer formula is drier or less effective.

Glowy, tinted sunscreen that fans wear as a radiant primer or light base, with little white cast. Many others find it greasy or too shimmery, and breakouts are a frequent complaint, along with pilling over moisturizer or makeup. Some say the tint looks orange or metallic on them, and a few report it separating.

Lightweight, sticky gel cream that many reviewers find hydrating and gentle, and it seems to suit oily or combination skin and warmer weather. A common caveat is that it is not enough alone for dry skin, so many layer a richer cream over it. A smaller group reports breakouts or irritation.

Gooey, hydrating essence that many reviewers love for soft, plump skin, and some say it calms redness. The main downside is breakouts, mostly small closed bumps, for a fair number of users, with some reporting stinging or dryness. Some layer a moisturizer over it.

Gentle, non-foaming cleanser that many reviewers say leaves dry and sensitive skin comfortable and not tight. Some get breakouts or irritation from it, and several feel it leaves a film or does not clean well, especially for makeup or sunscreen on its own. Best seen as a mild morning or second cleanse.

Rich, hydrating cream that many reviewers with dry skin love, usually as a night or winter moisturizer. Downsides are breakouts for some and a heavy, greasy feel, especially on oily skin or in humid weather. A noticeable fragrance bothers a few, while a small amount goes a long way.

Light, fast-absorbing lotion that many reviewers find hydrating and gentle, and some wear it morning and night. The main complaint is breakouts, often closed comedones, for a good number of users. Some find it not moisturizing enough for very dry skin, and a few noticed a different feel or irritation after a reformulation.

Cheap eye serum that many reviewers say reduces morning puffiness, though the effect is usually temporary. Results for dark circles are mixed, and dryness or irritation under the eyes is the main complaint. A few mention pilling under makeup or eye twitching, and many add moisturizer or eye cream over it.

Budget cleansing balm that many reviewers find gentle and soothing, and several say it melts makeup and sunscreen well as a first cleanse. Downsides are a greasy film that needs a second cleanse, breakouts or eye irritation for some, and a hard-to-squeeze tube with texture that can separate or turn grainy.

Thick but easy-spreading cream that many reviewers with dry, sensitive skin find hydrating and calming, especially in winter. The main complaints are irritation, stinging or burning for some, often blamed on eucalyptus oil, and breakouts for others. A few say a formula change stopped it working for them.

Moisturizer with sunscreen that a few reviewers like as a lightweight one-step product, but pilling is the main complaint, with many describing it balling up alone or under makeup. Breakouts, a greasy feel and a visible white cast also come up, and several switched to the PM lotion or a separate sunscreen.

Light, cooling gel that many reviewers with oily or combination skin find hydrating without greasiness. The main complaint is breakouts, followed by irritation and a strong scent in the regular version, with several preferring the fragrance-free one. Dry skin usually needs a richer cream on top, and a few report eyelid reactions.

Very lightweight sunscreen serum that many reviewers like for a dewy finish, little white cast and enough moisture to skip a moisturizer. Breakouts and stinging, mostly around the eyes, are the main complaints for a smaller group, and some find it shiny on oily skin. Several say newer bottles feel different.

Light, gel-like moisturizer that many reviewers with oily or combination skin like for daytime and under makeup. Price is a recurring complaint, and some find it too light for dry skin. A smaller group got breakouts or a shiny, greasy look.

Thick, soothing cream that many reviewers use on irritated, redness-prone skin and while using retinoids, and several prefer it to Cicaplast. The main downside is clogged pores and breakouts for a good number of users, and some find it too greasy or heavy, especially in summer.
